ba9ced61-2d7b-483a-9890-adcd597314b5.title: In Khimki wastelands turn into squares
claims: In Khimki starts the fourth season of the project "Name squares".
The authorities of the municipality and local entrepreneurs create public spaces on the site of abandoned territories, the press service of the Ministry of improvement of the Moscow region reported.
In Khimki, on the site of unused or abandoned territories, modern public spaces are created that are conducive to walking and recreation - "Namely Squares".
One of the most popular spaces in cities is increasingly becoming squares and parks.
After all, it is in the cities that the value of green spaces is felt most, said Mikhail Khaikin, Minister of Improvement of the Moscow Region.
For three seasons since the beginning of the project, 17 new squares appeared in Khimki.
Previously, in their place were wastelands or vice versa thick thickets of shrubs, which pedestrians bypassed.
The project is implemented according to a simple scheme: residents show the territory that needs improvement, and the local business community creates a modern space for recreation and walking.
For three years, “Nominal squares ” appeared in all neighborhoods of Khimki.
When creating them, certain criteria are necessarily observed: high-quality tiles, curbs, lawns, elegant and stylish benches, urns.
Also installed bright LED lights, CCTV cameras with connection to the system "Safe region", devices for charging gadgets, free Wi-Fi.
In addition, there is a place for a thematic platform: a workout, chess, a children ’ s town, a pond, a fountain.
The navigation stele closes the composition.

The project "Nominal squares" became the winner of the All-Russian competition "Urban Environment", held by the Ministry of Construction and Housing of Russia, and became one of the best municipal practices.
Well-equipped zones should become new centers of attraction for residents, Mikhail Khaikin emphasized.
The administration of Khimki said that they are already preparing for the fourth season of the project.
Residents and companies can offer their locations for new squares by sending an email to adm @ admhimki.ru, or leaving their application in the public reception of the municipality administration.

f0dd4b06-3c94-4607-8bff-3f3413294d72.title: In the United States, in the midst of the pandemic, the death rate from overdose reached a record 93 thousand
claims: In the United States, in the midst of the pandemic, overdose deaths reached a record 93 thousand.
In the United States, at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, 93,000 people died from overdoses.
The previous record in the country was set a year earlier, when 72,000 Americans were victims of drugs.
According to experts, coronavirus restrictions have isolated people suffering from drug addiction and made it difficult for them to access treatment.
In 1970, when the heroin epidemic raged in the United States, fewer than 7.2 thousand deaths were associated with an overdose.
At the height of the crack epidemic in 1988, about 9 thousand deaths were associated with an overdose.
Fentanyl, a dangerously potent opioid developed to treat severe pain caused by diseases such as cancer, has been supplanted other drugs in recent years.
Fentanyl is increasingly sold illegally and mixed with other drugs.
Fentanyl was responsible for more than 60% of overdose deaths last year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
In 2020, more than 3.3 million deaths were registered in the United States, 378 thousand of which are associated with COVID-19.
In Japan, more people died from suicide in a month than from COVID-19 complications in all of 2020.

957de1dd-666f-49d1-882c-751c133440ca.title: Le Figaro – quarantine or pandemic – scientists have found out what is worse
claims: Scientists have conducted an analysis to compare data from 94 countries and assess the relationship between strict quarantine measures and mortality in the pandemic era.
Data for the analysis came from 94 countries.
Researchers analyzed the impact of government restrictions on mortality rates, habitual health services, suicide rates, and mental health status.
Nowhere was there both high mortality and severe quarantine measures, and at the same time a low number of cases of COVID-19.
Australia or New Zealand had significant restrictions, but there was no high mortality.
Brazil, Sweden and Russia had small restrictions, but the mortality rate is high.
Quarantine can even reduce mortality compared with previous years, since common diseases such as the flu are less common and the number of accidents is reduced.
Government restrictions are linked to a reduction in routine visits to doctors.
The pandemic has affected the mental health of people, but the number of suicides has not increased.
In Japan, the increase in suicides is due to unemployment, and this happened after the return to normal life.
Funds earmarked for the fight against HIV and tuberculosis have been partially redirected to the coronavirus.
Government intervention has contributed to a reduction in deaths from COVID-19.
The quarantine cannot be worse than the damage from the pandemic, at least in the short term.

2c359466-cdbf-452f-a0f7-cf0df0795050.title: Cities in the north of France have restricted the sale of fuel through illegal migrants
claims: Cities on the northern coast of France have restricted the sale of take-away fuel to 10 liters per customer to stop illegal migration through the English Channel.
The purchase or sale of more than 10 litres of fuel - petrol or diesel - in hand-held containers is prohibited.
More fuel can be purchased only by those who need it for professional reasons.
The prefecture of the Pas-de-Calais department said the restriction was necessary given the "growing presence" of migrants seeking to cross the border illegally into the UK.
One of the main means of transportation through the English Channel are boats powered by a gasoline engine.
The restriction will be valid for two months and provides for the imposition of a fine of 135 euros and can grow to 3,700 euros in case of repeated violations.
British authorities recorded a new record of 430 illegal migrants per day arrived on the British coast on Monday.
The number of illegal migrants arriving in the UK in small boats this year has already exceeded the total number of arrivals for the whole of 2020.

7bb96a27-5c6c-465a-8f5c-a1181d4f8010.title: Ukrainian banks will be required to disclose full information about services
claims: The National Bank approved new requirements for disclosure by banks of information about services in advertising and on websites.
Banks need to change the information about services on websites and in advertising to meet the requirements.
The NBU gives financial institutions six months to adapt.
After three months, all banks must provide comprehensive information about the services on the site in a single unified format.
Banks must indicate the full cost of the service, including commissions to third parties and payments for additional services.
Banks must indicate the frequency of repayment of the loan, the conditions of early repayment, possible penalties in case of failure by the client to fulfill obligations.
The Financial Services Consumer Protection Department of the National Bank will start monitoring banks' compliance with these requirements in three months.
The legislation provides for penalties from 300 to 600 non-taxable minimum incomes of citizens for each case of failure to disclose information about services in full.
After six months, calculators should appear in the websites of banks to calculate expenses or income from the service.
After six months, new requirements for disclosure of information in advertising will be implemented.
Advertising should contain essential characteristics of the banking service, in particular, information about the full cost, conditions for obtaining the service, risks, etc.
The NBU recommends that financial institutions develop an automated database where all information about citizens’ appeals will be entered.
The NBU recommends that banks identify a responsible employee for reviewing each appeal, conduct training programs for bank employees who work with customers.

4e08eb04-e90f-4da0-8bb7-835f1da7ca98.title: Foreigners go to Russia for high-quality dentistry
claims: The Russian Association of Medical Tourism said that dentistry is the most common reason for visiting Russia among foreign patients.
44% of medical tourists come to Russia for dentistry.
Medical tourists visiting Russia for dentistry include citizens of the countries of the former USSR and Europeans.
The most demanded areas of dental care among foreign patients in Russia are orthodontics and surgical dentistry, namely implantation and prosthetics of teeth.
More than 20,000 foreign citizens visited Russia for medical purposes in 2016.
Over 100 foreign citizens visited the Eskulap clinic in Krasnodar for dentistry in 2016.
Patients most often complained of toothache, pulpitis, mild inflammation of the gums, especially in the winter.
Implantation and prosthetics of teeth is a popular dental service in Russia due to the affordable cost of imported implants.
Urology and gynecology are the second most popular medical tourism services in Russia, accounting for 23% of visits.
Parents from neighboring countries, Europe, and the UAE visit Russia for IVF due to its low cost, which is 2.5 times cheaper than elsewhere.
Plastic surgery is the third most popular medical tourism service in Russia, accounting for 17% of visits.
Plastic surgery services in Russia cost about 13% lower than elsewhere.
Orthopedics and Traumatology account for 11% of medical tourism visits to Russia.
Visitors to Russia are interested in the treatment of the hip, knee, and other joints.
Citizens of the Baltic States, the United States, France, and the United Kingdom visit Russia for complex orthopedic operations.
Cardiovascular surgery and ophthalmology share the fifth place in Russia's medical tourism ranking, accounting for 3% and 2% of visits, respectively.
Heart clinics in Moscow, Yekaterinburg, and St. Petersburg are leaders in cardiovascular surgery.
Prices for coronary bypass surgery and heart surgery in Russia are much lower than in foreign countries.
Ophthalmology services in Russia include laser correction of vision, treatment of glaucoma, and restoration of the retina.
Residents of the United States, Great Britain, and Israel are interested in ophthalmology services in Russia.

4851d0b2-c250-4ecf-bf47-503d7f448460.title: A million people will live on Mars!
claims: There are almost 50 projects of manned flights to Mars.
Elon Musk plans to transport a million people to Mars to create an independent civilization.
The company Srace X will begin the first flights of its space shuttles soon.
Elon Musk believes that resettling a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.
Life on Earth can be interrupted by factors such as supernova explosions, superflares, black holes, global epidemics, asteroid collisions, and man-made disasters.
A large colony of people on Mars will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.
Mars is better suited for human life compared to other celestial bodies in the solar system.
A day on Mars lasts 24 hours and 37 minutes, and its gravity is suitable for the human body.
There is water on Mars in the form of polar ice caps, which can be used for human settlement.
The minimum number of people required for a colony to become independent is one million.
This number of people will ensure the presence of specialists, stable population growth, and the ability to cope with diseases and epidemics.
Elon Musk proposes the term "terraforming" to describe the process of changing Mars' conditions to resemble those of Earth.
The first step in terraforming Mars is to melt the ice at the south pole, which will create a chain reaction and make the planet more habitable.
Technically, this can be achieved using nuclear charges or laser devices.
After liquid water appears on Mars, plants will be introduced to create oxygen and make the atmosphere breathable.
According to Elon Musk, the cultivation of "green lungs" and the creation of a livable air on Mars will take from 300 to 1000 years.
Elon Musk has listed the things and equipment needed for the first colonists, including devices for energy production and conversion.
The company Srace X considers the delivery of large numbers of light folding solar panels to Mars as a promising direction.
The total number of flights required to create a million-colony on Mars will be about 100 thousand.
Elon Musk has announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods to Mars should begin at the end of 2022.
By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching Mars in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.
The main obstacle to the implementation of this project is the high cost of a flight to Mars.
The cost of sending astronauts to Mars was estimated at $450 billion in 1989, but has been declining since then.
Elon Musk believes that the optimal cost for a flight to Mars should be around $500,000 per person.
SpaceX is working on creating a huge Mars Colonial Transporter rocket capable of lifting a spacecraft with 100 passengers into orbit.
The company is also developing a reusable interplanetary transport system to reduce the cost of each flight.
The ability to reuse spacecraft will reduce costs hundreds or even thousands of times.
Ensuring the safety of future colonists is one of the most important tasks, including protection from radiation and cosmic rays.
Scientists are working on solving the problems of radiation, cosmic rays, and weightlessness to ensure the safety of colonists.
Elon Musk has been recognized as one of the 75 most influential people of the 21st century for his efforts to make humanity a multi-planetary species.

63aff403-513b-4526-91ce-e298c7566415.title: All from Xiaomi: review of the Mi minimalist urban backpack and Mi multi-functional urban bags
claims: Xiaomi quickly expanded the list of branded accessories and equipment to unprecedented quantities.
The number of products with the Mi logo is comparable to what Samsung does.
Xiaomi has a range of products including "smart" house, small appliances for the kitchen and apartment, and clothes.
The Mi minimalist urban Backpack comes in a regular matte bag with a zip fastener.
The backpack is made of pleasant and rather dense polyester.
The backpack has a plastic frame sewn into the "front" part, which helps it keep a rectangular shape even when empty.
The back of the backpack is not the most ergonomic, but dense and stitched.
The straps of the backpack are of normal width, although not the thickest.
The zippers of the backpack work perfectly and look reliable, with comfortable plastic "tongues" with the Mi logo.
The backpack has a small inscription "Urban life style" on the front.
The backpack has over a dozen different pockets, pockets, and compartments.
The main drawback of the backpack is that if you put something in all the pockets, the volume of internal space will greatly decrease.
Xiaomi does not name the volume of the backpack, only the dimensions (30 x 14 x 39 cm).
The estimated volume of the backpack is around 15-20 liters.
The backpack was tested for about a month and held its shape, with intact seams.
The length of the straps of the backpack is a couple of centimeters shorter than expected.
The backpack has a comfortable handle, which is especially useful in public transport.
The manufacturer claims a water-repellent impregnation for the backpack.
The Mi minimalist urban bag is a classic sling made of the same fabric as the backpack.
The sling has similar zippers to the backpack and comes in a package.
The sling is noticeably smaller than it looks in the pictures, with dimensions of 17.5 x 8 x 32 cm and a volume of about 4 liters.
The sling has a good set of pockets, including one outer small zippered inner compartment and two quite large pockets without clasps.
The back of the sling is mesh, and the single strap can be fixed both on the left and right.
The capacity of the sling leaves much to be desired, making it suitable only for carrying small items.
The sling has a noticeable "Chinese for the Chinese" tailoring, with the strap ending somewhere on the shoulder.
Xiaomi has a couple of good products, with the backpack being comfortable and suitable for carrying a medium format laptop and small items.
The price of the Mi minimalist urban backpack seems justified.
The sling left a rather controversial impression, being an inexpensive option for carrying a minimum of necessary items.

claims: The Stratolaunch Model 351 carrier aircraft is the largest aircraft in history, having a wingspan of 117 m and a length of 73 m.

The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is equipped with six twin-circuit Pratt & Whitney PW4056 turbojet engines with a thrust of 25 tons.

The maximum range of the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft with full load will not exceed 3700 km.

The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is designed to be used as a carrier for the aerospace system Stratolaunch, created by the American company Stratolaunch Systems.

The project of the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft was announced in December 2011.

The start of commercial launches from the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft will be possible from 2020.
The Orbital ATK Pegasus XL light launch vehicle is considered as a payload option for the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft.
The Orbital ATK Pegasus XL launch vehicle has a starting mass of 23.2 tons, payload mass load of 443 kg.
The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft has the possibility of carrying and launching from it in one flight up to three Pegasus XL launch vehicles.

eb9efcc0-426d-4d13-8b59-7ec8df69d303.title: Scientists have proven that there can be life on Mars
claims: Scientists have proven that there can be life on Mars.
Dr. Jean-Pierre Paul De Vera from the German Center for Spatial Research in Berlin conducted an experiment to create a camera that fully reproduces the conditions of life on Mars.
The experiment confirmed that organisms living on Earth can use Mars as a natural habitat.
NASA has long sought to explore the possibility of life on Mars due to the planet’s resemblance to Earth.
Recent advances show that water once flowed on the red planet, which means that Mars was once adapted to the existence of life in conditions with a warmer and wetter climate.
Dr. Jean-Pierre Paul De Vera proved that living organisms can survive and thrive in the current conditions of the red planet.
His research was presented on the program “Tomorrow’s world” on Amazon Prime.
The "Mars chamber" was organized with all the conditions inherent in Mars, including temperature, atmospheric pressure, chemical composition, and ultraviolet rays.
The experiment tested the resistance of terrestrial organisms to Martian conditions for nine days with microorganisms brought from Antarctica.
The microorganisms not only survived but also began to thrive in the Martian environment.
Microorganisms are able to survive on Mars, including bacteria and organisms that use photosynthesis.
Life is possible on Mars today, and Mars could be a habitat for organisms that live on Earth.
The next step for scientists is to modify the Red Planet to make it more adapted for growing vegetable crops.
NASA’s concept of colonizing Mars in the future has every reason for life and is planned to be implemented in three separate phases by the mid-2030s.

b1ce6db5-43e6-4401-a8e4-e0e5cc669955.title: Drought and a catastrophically low harvest: what did the summer heat bring to Europe?
claims: Europe's summer heat turned the usually green pastures and gardens into a scorched, arid landscape in brown tones.
Drought, especially in the northern and central regions of the continent, has had a devastating impact on farm crops.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) reported that the drought was caused by prolonged periods of hot weather, record high temperatures, and catastrophically low rainfall in the first half of the summer.
April and May were the warmest spring months in Europe, according to long-term observations.
June and July temperatures were well above average, especially in the Nordic countries.
Temperatures exceeded 30 ° C in the Arctic Circle, with Norway reaching a record level of 33.5 ° C on July 17.
Finland experienced the hottest July on record.
Precipitation levels were extremely low, with extensive areas of “extreme aridity” stretching from Belgium and the Netherlands to Finland and Estonia.
Scientists point to a combination of several factors, including global climate change and a zone of increased atmospheric pressure, as the cause of the drought in Europe.
The EU plan to combat climate change was prepared in 2015, but has not been updated since the conclusion of the Paris climate agreement.

The level of ambition does not correspond to the stated goal of the Paris Agreement, which is to keep the growth of average annual temperatures at a level not higher than 1.5 ° C in the next 30 years.
Brussels has eased regulation and sped up payments to drought-stricken farmers, allowing them to receive up to 70% of direct subsidies and 85% of aid for rural development in mid-October.
Farmers across Europe are preparing for one of the worst harvests in history, with yields of some vegetable crops expected to drop by 50%.
German potato chip manufacturers are concerned that a drought could lead to a shortage of potatoes needed for industrial production of chips.
Analysts at Strategyie Grains said wheat and barley yields in Germany and Scandinavia this year could be assessed as "catastrophic".
Grain yields declined in France, Italy, the United Kingdom, and countries in Central and Southeast Europe.
Sweden's wheat harvest could fall by more than 40% this year due to dry and hot weather.
Finland's farmers suffered losses due to wet and cold weather last year, and this summer are seriously affected by drought.
Temperatures in early August approached 30 ° C in Finland, although the average in August is 19 ° C.
Many parts of England and Wales have not seen rain since the end of May, creating conditions of "increased flammability".
About 65% of arable land in Poland has been affected by drought.
May in Poland was the warmest in the last 55 years.
Germany's May temperatures were the highest since 1881.
The grain harvest in Germany is expected to fall by 20% due to drought.
According to forecasts, the grain harvest in Estonia may be lost by 30% to 70% this summer.
The government of Estonia has allocated 20 million euros to farmers affected by the drought.
The drought in Latvia was declared a "national disaster" in June.
Farmers in Latvia are selling cattle due to a lack of feed.
Lithuania's government declared a national emergency in July due to the drought.
The yield of agricultural crops in Lithuania decreased by 15-50% compared to the level of 2006.
Switzerland's federal government is cutting import tariffs on livestock feed to help farmers fight drought.
The Swiss army carried out an operation to deliver water by air for cows in high-altitude pastures affected by hot weather.
Denmark's spring harvest of cereals and vegetables decreased by 40-50% due to drought.
The losses will cost Denmark's agricultural industry 8.5 billion Swedish kroner [about 828 million euros].

e7e49238-e932-4dde-a2e6-0280531a2e6e.title: Pandora's Box by Konstantin Nikiforov. Pesticide Roundup is now a Bayer Group problem?
claims: The French government approved the decision of the American jury, which sentenced the biotechnology corporation Monsanto to pay $289 million to American Dwayne Johnson.
Dwayne Johnson, who worked as a gardener, claims that due to the use of anti-weeds Roundup and RangerPro containing glycol Fosat, he got cancer.
State Secretary of the French Ministry of Ecology, Brune Poiarson, commented on the decision: “We did not wait for the historic decision of the American court to take action.
France voted against the extension of the permit for the use of glyphosate in Europe, and we are trying to mobilize other European states to share our position.
French Environment Minister Nicolas Hulot called on Europeans and Americans to take part in the “war against pesticides”.
The decision of the California court was also welcomed by the Confederation of French Peasants.
Laurent Pinatel, a representative of the Confederation, recalled Emmanuel Macron’s promise to ban the use of pesticides by 2021.
Despite France’s efforts, the European Commission recently extended the license for glyphosate for another five years.
Glyphosate due to its cheapness and ease of use is very widespread and is often used to control weeds.
In 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer and the WHO Cancer Agency concluded that the substance is “probably carcinogenic to humans”.
The lawsuit of Dewayne Johnson, who was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma in 2014, is the first glyphosate case to go to trial.
In the United States, Monsanto has already filed about five thousand similar lawsuits.

German pharmaceutical group Bayer, which recently acquired the Monsanto group, continues to argue that the herbicide Roundup is “reliable and not carcinogenic” and is going to appeal the court’s decision.
Bayer closed the acquisition of Monsanto in June 2018.
Shares of the American company will no longer be traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), as Bayer became the sole owner of Monsanto.
Monsanto shareholders will receive a payment of $128 per share of the company.
Werner Baumann, Chairman of the Board of Management of Bayer, said that the acquisition will increase the value of the company and help farmers increase the production of quality food.
Bayer expects the acquisition to make a positive contribution to core earnings per share starting in 2019, with a double-digit percentage from 2021.
As for the verdict on glyphosate in California on August 10, 2018, Bayer believes that the jury’s decision contradicts the weight of scientific evidence.
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) confirmed that glyphosate does not cause cancer.

The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) and other regulatory bodies around the world have also concluded that glyphosate can be used safely.
The jury’s verdict is only the first step in this case, and it remains the subject of post-trial motions in the court of first instance and appeal.
Bayer has been able to actively engage in advocacy efforts in glyphosate trials and any other legal disputes.
CEO Werner Baumann said: “We will actively defend this case and all pending cases”.
As of the end of July, the number of plaintiffs in both state and federal lawsuits is approximately 8,000.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) says glyphosate is unlikely to be carcinogenic.
Glyphosate is an active ingredient in Monsanto’s Roundup, which is the most popular weed killer in the US.

20add5c9-d887-4d1e-bd93-7de08d930203.title: Scientists have estimated the loss of agriculture from insects due to warming
claims: American scientists have estimated the loss of world agriculture from insect pests, the activity of which will increase due to global warming.
Annual wheat crop losses will reach 59 million tonnes against the current production of 749.4 million tonnes.
The loss of wheat, rice, and corn will be about 213 million tons.
Global climate change will lead to more frequent and intense droughts, dangerous for crops.
Warming can “reshape ” the map of world agriculture, shifting the boundaries of regions where the climate allows you to grow certain varieties of plants.
Curtis Deutsch, from the University of Washington, has estimated how much increased insect activity will affect crops of rice, corn and wheat.
Rice, corn, and wheat are three key crops for about 4 billion people, according to statistics from the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
In 2016, 749.4 million tons of wheat, 740 million tons of rice and 1.06 billion tons of corn were grown worldwide.
Warming exponentially increases the rate of metabolism in insects.
Warming will increase the rate of insect reproduction everywhere except the tropics.
Scientists used data from previous laboratory experiments and observations on the influence of temperature on the metabolism and reproduction of 38 species of insect pests.
Each additional degree of future warming will lead to an increase in annual crop losses by 10-25 percent.
The relatively safe two-degree warming scenario would result in losses of approximately 213 million tonnes per year.
Corn yields will be reduced by 31%, rice by 19% and wheat by 46% under the two-degree warming scenario.
The United States, China and France will suffer the most from the losses of wheat, rice, and corn.
To combat the increased activity of insects, all the technologies of modern agriculture will be needed, including pesticides, the use of GMOs and practices like crop rotation.
Even with modern agricultural technologies, "insects still win" in most warming scenarios.
The authors' model may underestimate crop losses due to the fact that many insects simultaneously carry pathogens dangerous to crops.

Warming will affect the natural enemies of insects, and they will be affected by other factors of climate change, such as changes in rainfall patterns or more frequent periods of extreme temperatures.
If humanity does not start taking measures to combat climate change before 2035, it will not be able to limit the increase in global average temperature to a safe two degrees Celsius.
Even if humanity complies with the Paris Agreement, the average temperature on Earth can still rise by another 3-4 degrees due to irreversible climatic processes that will trigger warming.

6d5d3f6b-9387-478b-8989-a4c4b56a23e3.title: Japan withdraws from International Whaling Commission
claims: Japan will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in 2019.
The Japanese delegation spoke in September at the IWC conference for the abolition of the ban on whaling for commercial purposes.
Japan intends to resume whaling in territorial waters from July.
The population of the northern smooth whale in the Atlantic is sharply declining due to human activities.
Japan has refrained from whaling for 30 years.
The moratorium on commercial whaling was introduced in 1986 to restore the whale population.
Japan has proposed the establishment of a committee to deal with balanced fishing (including commercial whaling and aboriginal fishing).
According to the rules of the IWC, Japan will officially leave the Commission on June 30, if the decision is notified before January 1.

43224d62-a953-4308-a385-8913a5ef83a6.title: Mysterious details of famous masterpieces of art
claims: Art historian BBC Culture explains the mysterious details of the most famous works of art.
Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring" has a pearl that is only a figment of the viewer's imagination.
The pearl in Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring" is an optical illusion created by two light strokes of the brush.
There is no fastener that connects the jewelry with the girl's ear in Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring".
The earring itself in Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring" is an illusion created by the viewer's imagination from two barely noticeable curls of white paint.
The golden hair of the goddess in Sandro Botticelli's "Birth of Venus" forms a curl of an ideal spiral shape.
The ideal logarithmic spiral of the curl in Botticelli's "Birth of Venus" is not an accident.
The rotational vector of the curl in Botticelli's "Birth of Venus" repeats the movements of the wind gods Zephyr and Chloride.
Hieronymus Bosch's "Garden of Earthly Delights" has an egg balanced on the head of a rider that reveals the true meaning of the work.
The egg in Bosch's "Garden of Earthly Delights" symbolizes the world being born and broken.
William Turner's "Rain, Steam and Speed" has a hare hidden on the left side of the canvas that symbolizes rebirth and hope.
The hare in Turner's "Rain, Steam and Speed" honors the memory of the victims of a train tragedy.
Georges Sera's "Bathers in Agnères" was completed in 1884 and later improved using the pointillism style.
The theory of color in Sera's "Bathers in Agnères" is related to the ideas of the French chemist Michel Eugène Chevreul.
The chimneys in the background of Sera's "Bathers in Agnères" belong to a factory that produced candles using Chevrel's technology.
Edvard Munch's "The Scream" was possibly inspired by a huge electric light bulb filled with 20,000 small ones at the 1889 World Exhibition in Paris.
The face in Munch's "The Scream" reflects the lowered jaw and bulbous skull of the electric totem of Edison.
Gustav Klimt's "Kiss" has patterns on the woman's dress that resemble petri dishes with cages.
Klimt's "Kiss" explores the soul of a woman in love under a microscope.
Klimt's "Kiss" is a vivid biopsy of eternal love.

2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9.title: Death in the garden: an American corporation found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide
claims: Monsanto, the world's largest producer of chemicals for the agro-industrial complex, was found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide.
Alberta and Alva Pilliod, an elderly couple from California, won a lawsuit against Monsanto after being diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Monsanto's Roundup herbicide, which contains the active ingredient glyphosate, was first synthesized by Monsanto employee John Franz in 1970.

The International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate in 2015.
The Pilliod couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto in 2017, which was accelerated due to their poor health.
The jury decided that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks of using Roundup, and ordered the company to pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages.
This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.
Bayer, the German concern that owns Monsanto, said it does not agree with the decision and will appeal.
The US Supreme Court ruled in 2016 that the amount of a fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.
The Pilliod couple will receive a maximum of $495 million in addition to their compensatory $55 million, if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments.
Monsanto's lawyers argued that their products were harmless, citing research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

US Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said that glyphosate is needed to feed 10 billion people by 2050.
Monsanto's defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, which the company claimed showed that glyphosate was safe.
However, internal correspondence between Monsanto employees and EPA officials showed that the company had attempted to influence the agency's findings.
A federal employee noted that if he could "kill" glyphosate research, he would "deserve a medal."
The Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, despite initial plans to do so.
The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.
In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.
Bayer is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products, and faces around 130,000 similar claims in the United States.
Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.
Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, Bayer has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.
Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite concerns over its safety.
EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years in 2017, despite initial plans to ban it.
In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds and plant protection products, and the herbicide Roundup is widely available.

951a0400-5f9c-4e80-bb5c-fc38f843de27.title: To the British shores - by boat
claims: More and more migrants are risking their lives trying to cross the English Channel and get from France to the UK in small boats.
Refugees have stormed trucks going to the UK, hid in trucks at the entrance to the tunnel under the English Channel, or hoped to travel on ferries plying between the two shores.
The French police are doing everything possible to ensure that migrants on this side of the strait are not detained.
Every day, the natural settlements of migrants are cleaned up.
People from Iraq, Iran, Afghanistan, Syria and Africa go to the city, taking their property, during inspections.
The police carry out operations every day, asking people to move their tents a couple of meters.
If it turns out that there is no one in the tent, the police dismantle it, seize things, phones, papers.
This strategy is designed to prevent the expansion of informal settlements into giant camps, such as the "Jungle" camp, which existed in Calais a few years ago.
Migrants are increasingly agreeing to a new service from smugglers - to sail to the UK on a boat.
This type of transport is becoming more and more popular: it is cheaper, and with it there is a greater chance of success.
In February alone, British rescuers assisted 200 refugees in 48 hours, among them children.
Last year, the French authorities tried to intervene in relation to almost 3 thousand people crossing the English Channel, which is 17 times more than in 2016.
Almost 2 thousand refugees reached the British coast, 125 were expelled from the country, the rest settled, at least temporarily.
Migrants refuse the help of the French border guards, and they have no right to insist - the use of force in the water can turn into tragedy, people resist.
Boats are brought in trucks from England, and then taken to France.
These boats go without a navigator, without a rudder and wind, and are pushed away from the shore.
So far, 2-3 deaths have been recorded, but there is a risk of a real large-scale disaster.
In 2016, the French authorities razed the infamous spontaneous refugee camp in Calais, nicknamed the “Jungle”.
People were resettled, but many remained on the coast, with hundreds of migrants settling in an old warehouse complex in Dunkirk.
There are about 800 people in the warehouse complex, with a fire on the ground floor, and a family with children warming up near it.
The refugees are from Iraq, and are waiting for a seat in the boat, for which they will have to pay from 2 to 3 thousand pounds per person.
The main thing is to get to the British territorial waters, but the authorities are improving tracking systems, strengthening the patrol.
Those who were able to survive the journey and bypass the patrol in the UK fall into special centers, where they are accepted by volunteers.
Volunteers provide language courses, assistance in solving domestic and legal issues.

Refugees are arriving in the UK at a time when anti-migrant sentiment is growing, with the slogan “We have lost control of our borders” becoming one of the main reasons for the mobilization of supporters of“ Brexit”.
The authorities are required to expel illegal refugees from the country.
Brigitte Chapman, who represents the migrant support organisation, thinks people with good reasons for asylum should be able to apply on the French side of the strait.

82379bc3-74e0-4dbd-95d1-1686d1a2318c.title: The assembly of an important element of the international thermonuclear reactor ITER began in Russia
claims: The assembly of an important element of the international thermonuclear reactor ITER began in Russia
Sredne-Nevsky Shipyard began assembling the coil of the poloidal field PF1 — an important element of the international experimental fusion reactor ITER under construction in France
The ITER reactor is being built near the Cadarache Research Center in southern France jointly by the European Union, Russia, China, India, Japan, South Korea and the United States
The ITER project will be the first large-scale attempt to demonstrate the feasibility of using a fusion reaction to generate energy on an industrial scale
If the ITER project is successful, humanity will be able to count on the possession of an almost inexhaustible source of energy
The PF1 coil is one of six poloidal field coils in the magnetic system that serves to hold the plasma in the ITER reactor
The coil is a complex product, the basis of which are eight superconducting two-layer double-start gallets
The winding of each of the gallets was carried out simultaneously from two cables
For each of the 16 cables of the PF1 coil, a niobium-titanium superconductor made earlier in Russia in cooperation with Europe was used
The niobium-titanium superconductor has superconducting properties at ultra-low temperatures
The completion of the production of the PF1 coil and its dispatch to the site of the ITER installation is scheduled for 2021

e76662d6-f9a5-4ed8-8cdb-93d0bafdf900.title: The answer is: URGENT!! PLEASE!!! “The motto of Hemingway ’ s hero can be: to survive in hopelessness. ” Do you share that opinion? Argue your point of view.
claims: The work of E. Hemingway represents a new step forward in the development of American and world realistic art.
The main theme of the work of E. Hemingway throughout his life remained the theme of the tragedy of the fate of an ordinary American.
The soul of his novels are action, struggle, daring.
The author admires proud, strong, human heroes who are able to preserve dignity in the most difficult circumstances.
Many heroes of E. Hemingway are doomed to hopeless loneliness, to despair.
Journalism helped him develop a basic principle: never write about what you do not know.
He did not tolerate chatter and preferred to describe simple physical actions, leaving room for the feelings in the subtext.
He believed that there is no need to talk about feelings, emotional states, it is enough to describe the actions in which they arose.
His prose is the canvas of the external life of people, of being, containing the greatness and insignificance of feelings, desires and motives.

The “iceberg principle ” put forward by the writer is combined with the so-called“ side view ” – the ability to see thousands of tiny details that seem not directly related to events, but actually play a huge role in the text, recreating the flavor of time and place.
A real triumph awaited him in 1952, when he published his novel The Old Man and the Sea.
The Old Man and the Sea is full of biblical grandeur and sorrow, and is deeply humane.
The book embodies love for man, faith in his strength in its broad, generalized, almost symbolic images.
The writer talks about the dignity of a person, about the bitterness and happiness of the winner, who was left with the skeleton of a fish eaten by sharks in The Old Man and the Sea.

74f8fd2b-ef87-460d-b642-54e499183a9e.title: The consequences of isolation: the coronavirus pandemic could lead to a wave of suicides
claims: The COVID-19 pandemic appears to be on the decline.
Statistics say that the number of new cases of infection in the world is gradually decreasing.
The number of deaths from COVID-19 is also decreasing.
As of May 15, more than 4,527,000 people have been infected.
More than 303 thousand infected died.
Almost 1 million 706 thousand patients recovered.
2 million 518 thousand cases remain active.
Less than 46,000 patients are in critical condition.
This is 2% of the total number of active cases.
If we consider completed cases, the mortality rate has already decreased to 15%.
Europe is the first country to declare the end of the COVID-19 epidemic, which is Slovenia.
Doctors warn of an extremely serious and dangerous side effect of the pandemic, which is about mental health.
The isolation is unbearable for some people, leading to thoughts of suicide.
The finance minister of the federal state of Hesse committed suicide due to concerns about the economic impact of the epidemic.
A doctor at a football club in Reims committed suicide after learning that he had a positive test for coronavirus while in quarantine.
The COVID-19 pandemic has a significant effect on mental health, which could lead to a rise in suicide rates.
Some crises, such as periods of war, can have a protective effect on the population and reduce the suicide rate.
The 9/11 attacks led to a decrease in suicide rates in New York City due to increased social cohesion.
The same mechanism manifested itself in France in 1998, when the national team won the World Cup, leading to a 10.3% drop in the number of suicides.
Group unity and social cohesion can have a protective effect on mental health.
The 1918-19 Spanish flu pandemic dramatically increased suicide rates in the United States.
The SARS epidemic in Hong Kong led to an explosive increase in suicides among the elderly, with a 15% increase for those over 65.
Isolation has a direct effect on the brain, increasing the risk of mortality and suicidality.
Functional MRI shows that social isolation leads to a change in the functioning of certain brain regions in individuals with suicidal tendencies.
The psychological impact of isolation has already been demonstrated during previous epidemics, such as SARS and Ebola.
The Lancet notes an increase in post-traumatic stress and depression, which lasts up to three years after the epidemic.
Economic instability and unemployment can contribute to an increase in suicide rates, with a 20-30% increase in suicide rates due to sharp increases in unemployment.
COVID-19 puts tens of millions of people at risk of unemployment, which can lead to an increase in suicide rates.
Medical records show that every suicide committed is accompanied by 20 suicide attempts.
A study examined the mental health of Belgians after a month of quarantine and found significant increases in anxiety and depressive disorders.
Women and young people between the ages of 16 and 24 were the most affected by anxiety and depressive disorders.
The presence of loved ones and professional activities can have a protective effect on mental health.
The explosive growth in arms sales during the current crisis raises concerns about the exponential increase in the number of suicides with the use of firearms.
The presence of weapons in the house can increase the likelihood of suicide with the use of firearms by 10 times.

3df0ec8d-9ccb-4295-9146-9c845e14d444.title: Why 35 countries are building the world ’ s largest fusion reactor
claims: The 1985 meeting of the heads of the USA and the USSR gave the world one of the most ambitious technological projects: the experimental thermonuclear reactor ITER.
Thermonuclear fusion has long stirred minds as a potential source of energy.
In theory, thermonuclear power plants can be four times more efficient than modern nuclear power plants, while much cleaner and safer.
Thermonuclear power plants have no problems with uncontrolled chain reactions and highly radioactive waste, and the fuel can be sea water.
The multibillion-dollar project ITER is being worked on by the EU, the US, Russia, India, China, South Korea, and Japan.
ITER will work at the end of 2025, forty years after the negotiations of Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev in Geneva.
Thermonuclear energy tries to copy the processes that occur inside stars, where nuclei of hydrogen isotopes merge and release huge energy.
To achieve thermonuclear energy on Earth, special conditions are needed, such as temperatures 10 times higher than in the core of the Sun.
ITER is based on a tokamak, a toroidal vacuum chamber with magnetic coils, which is the most common scheme used for thermonuclear fusion.
The first tokamaks appeared in the USSR in the 1960s, and the largest tokamak in the world will be built for ITER.
In tokamak, deuterium and tritium are launched and heated to temperatures over 150 million degrees Celsius.
The gas turns into plasma, which is kept at a distance from the walls by a magnetic field, and a current is passed through the plasma itself.
A powerful magnetic field is provided by superconducting magnets, which need to be cooled in a vacuum chamber to almost absolute zero, -268 ° C.
Modern tokamaks emit less energy than is spent on heating the system, and it is not possible to adapt them to generate energy.
The best result is the British JET, which returns up to 67% of the energy spent.
ITER will be a huge structure, with a height of a nine-storey house and a diameter of about the same size, and is expected to release energy ten times more than is spent on heating plasma.
ITER will not produce electricity, but will use all the allocated energy to heat the walls of the tokamak.
The next stage of the project, DEMO, will be a prototype fusion reactor for power plants, which is expected to appear in the 2040-50s.
India, Russia, South Korea, and Japan have expressed their desire to build such reactors.
The most important goal of ITER is to show the possibility of generating energy by a fusion reactor.
ITER should demonstrate the controlled production of "burning plasma" and the self-reproduction of tritium, a fairly rare isotope used as a fuel.
ITER should also demonstrate how ready modern technologies are for the construction of commercial thermonuclear power plants, as well as assess their reliability and safety.
Safety is one of the key advantages of fusion reactors over conventional nuclear reactors, as a chain reaction with consequences is impossible.
The radioactivity of the fuel in fusion reactors is also much lower, with tritium being a weak source of beta radiation.
The design of the reactor involves several barriers for radioactive substances arising in the process of operation.
The half-life of radioactive waste for most isotopes in a fusion reactor is about 10 years, compared to thousands or millions of years for spent nuclear fuel.
The project ITER began in 1985, with a meeting between the leaders of the United States and the USSR, and the treaty was signed in 1986 by Euroatom, the USSR, the United States, and Japan.
Work on the design of ITER began in 1988 and continued until the approval of the final version in 2001.
China and South Korea joined the consortium to work on ITER in 2003, and India joined in 2005.
The site for the construction of ITER was chosen in 2005, near the Cadarache nuclear energy research center in Provence, France.
The interstate agreement on the establishment of ITER was signed by the ministers of the participating countries on November 21, 2006.
The ITER Organization began its work in October 2007, and the site preparation started in 2007, with construction beginning in 2010.
As of the end of June 2019, the project was ready by more than 63%, with more than 70% of the buildings completed and the first components of the reactor installed.
ITER surpasses many large-scale scientific buildings of the century, including the Large Hadron Collider, in terms of complexity and manufacturability.
The project budget was initially estimated at €5 billion, but has already crossed the mark of €20 billion.
Alternative methods for thermonuclear fusion are being studied, including the stellarator and inertial retention.
Start-ups such as Commonwealth Fusion Systems and Tri Alpha Energy are working on alternative approaches to thermonuclear fusion.
Critics believe that fusion is too expensive and commercially inefficient, and call for investment in renewable energy instead.
ITER emphasizes that the creation of new clean energy sources with a constant level of generation remains an important task.
Thermonuclear energy will not replace renewable energy, but will serve as an alternative to traditional “dirty” energy sources.
The first launch of ITER is scheduled for December 2025, with the expectation of achieving a tenfold return on power by 2035.

ae697222-c58e-45c3-a537-fcecfe6ba502.title: The story of Ernest Hemingway ’ s third wife, who left him so as not to be a footnote in someone else ’ s biography
claims: Martha Gellhorn is the third wife of Ernest Hemingway, also known as the distinguished war correspondent of the twentieth century.
Gellhorn herself would prefer to be remembered as a brilliant journalist, rather than as the wife of a writer.
She is the only woman of all Ernest Hemingway, who decided not only to leave him, but also considered herself no less talented.
Martha Gellhorn and Ernest Hemingway met in late 1936 at a restaurant in Key West, Florida.
At the time of their meeting, Hemingway was already at the top of his popularity thanks to the novel “Farewell to Arms!” and other books.

Martha Gellhorn was a 28-year-old writer who had returned from Paris, where she worked in the glamorous magazine Vogue, experienced an unsuccessful romance with a married man, wrote a book of reports about the times of economic depression and even worked in the presidential administration.
Similar views on politics and a love of writing led to a friendship between Martha Gellhorn and Ernest Hemingway.
Hemingway offered Martha a business trip to New York, then together to go to Spain, where at the time there were civil unrest.
The acquaintance with the writer determined the whole future life of Gellhorn, both personal and professional: it was he who prompted her to become a military reporter.
Before the joint trip to Spain, Martha Gellhorn was not in love with Ernest Hemingway.
In Spain, passion broke out between Martha Gellhorn and Ernest Hemingway.
After finishing work in Spain, the couple settled in Cuba.
Martha Gellhorn and Ernest Hemingway got married four years after they met, but by that time their relationship had already soured.
The main reason for the end of their relationship is Martha’s desire to continue to cover important events in Europe, but Ernest Hemingway wanted to see her only as the home Mrs. Hemingway.
At the end of 1943, Martha Gellhorn left for Europe and again found herself in the epicenter of military events.
On May 25, 1944, Ernest Hemingway was in an accident - his drunk friend got behind the wheel and crashed the car.
Martha Gellhorn immediately arrived at the hospital, but saw her husband surrounded by cheerful friends and empty bottles of alcohol.
Ernest Hemingway’s decision to work for Collier’s Weekly magazine was the last straw for Martha Gellhorn.
Martha Gellhorn went to Europe without the official documents of the journalist and tricked into a ship headed for France, posing as a nurse.
Once on board, Martha Gellhorn found the nearest toilet and locked herself inside.
Her ship crossed the English Channel and arrived in France on the morning of June 8.
After landing on the shore, Martha Gellhorn forgot that she was a journalist, and began to help the wounded.
The family broke up in 1945, and after that, Martha did not allow anyone to mention the name of her ex-husband in her presence.
Martha Gellhorn was unhappy that first of all she was perceived as the former wife of the writer Ernest Hemingway, and only then as a talented reporter.
Over 60 years of journalism, Martha Gellhorn has not lost a sense of compassion for the victims of conflict, reminding his readers that the fate of real people is hidden behind the battle statistics.
Martha Gellhorn was 87 when she last worked as a correspondent.
Almost until the age of 89, she was engaged in scuba diving and dreamed of traveling to Egypt to look at the pyramids.
In 2012, a film about the relationship of Martha Gellhorn and Ernest Hemingway was released with Nicole Kidman and Clive Owen.
In 2020, author Paula MacLaine’s book Love and Ashes was published, which also tells about the great love and hatred that followed between two strong personalities.
Martha Gellhorn had all the qualities of a true journalist.
A memorial plaque dedicated to Martha Gellhorn as a war correspondent was opened in her London house.
Martha Gellhorn said, “I’ve been a writer for over 40 years. I was a writer before I met him, and I was a writer after I left him. Why should I just be a footnote in someone’s life?”

Salt water, or brine, with impurities that allow it to remain in a liquid state at low temperature and pressure, is particularly attractive for use in applications.
The first traces of brine with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015.
A reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of Mars in 2018, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.
Planetary scientists confirmed that lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.
Pralay Gayen and colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.
The installation used a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide.
Lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ was used as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production, and platinum on activated carbon was used as an electrocatalyst for hydrogen production.
A commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator in the installation.
The installation produced oxygen and hydrogen with a current output of 70 percent and energy efficiency in the range of 36 to 70 percent.
The installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst, with no traces of ruthenium found in the solution after 300-minute operation.
The rate of oxygen production was compared to MOXIE values and found to be 25 times more efficient with the same energy supply.
The developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require subsequent purification, unlike MOXIE, which produces carbon monoxide that must be filtered.

SpaceX plans to develop equipment that produces resources and energy on Mars.

044d3c5a-4cb5-4bbc-b6a1-7f14276d4f55.title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
claims: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars.
Cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.
Cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen.
Cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust.
Cyanobacteria can be used to feed other microbes.
All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.
The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent).
Cyanobacteria can fix carbon dioxide and nitrogen, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients.
Atmospheric pressure on Mars is less than 1% of Earth’s.
The total pressure on Mars is from 6 to 11 GPa.
The partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen on Mars is from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa.
Researchers have developed a bioreactor called Atmos with an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth’s.
The bioreactor Atmos uses 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.
The bioreactor Atmos includes water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice.
The bioreactor Atmos includes a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created using only what can be found on Mars.
Nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.
Cyanobacteria can be used to obtain sugar, amino acids and other nutrients to feed other crops.
Cyanobacteria can be used for the production of medicines.
The bioreactor Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions.
The bioreactor system could one day save human life on Mars.

1394885a-470f-454f-b469-f1ca5fcce384.title: NASA rover with “oxygen generator ” began landing on the Red planet

e8246944-602a-40a0-ab1d-9dd12d05a509.title: How India ’ s rice production can adapt to climate change challenges
claims: India’s rice production can adapt to climate change challenges by applying new management methods to maintain production and increase yields.
Rice is a staple crop in India, China, and other Southeast Asian countries.
Rice consumption is on the rise in the U.S. and elsewhere.
The production and processing of 1 kilogram of rice takes about 4,000 liters of water.
Climate change could affect the availability of water in the future, impacting rice production.
By 2050, the world population will grow by two billion people, and the demand for food will grow by 60%.
The world will need more water for crop production, drinking water, and industrial use by 2050.
Farmers in Bihar, India, grow rice during the rainy season, when heavy rainfall allows for a good harvest.
Weather changes affect temperature, rainfall, and carbon dioxide concentrations, which are important for crop growth, especially rice.
The stage of crop growth is decreasing, and the time of full maturity becomes shorter due to climate change.
Crops ripen faster, and as a result, the full potential of the crop is not used.
If farmers continue their current practices, rice yields will drop significantly by 2050.
Direct-sown rice instead of seedlings can increase production by using significantly less water.
Soil protection technologies, such as keeping plant residues on the ground, can reduce evaporation and preserve water.
Implementing strategies to prevent post-harvest losses can further improve crop availability and food security.
FAO estimates that about 30% of the crop is lost or discarded after harvest.
The best approach to increase rice production by 60% while minimizing additional irrigation needs is to combine conservation strategies and reduce 30% post-harvest losses.

84b626c1-2d10-4f0b-b53d-dc66f0f5b5a0.title: Why Lyuli with Covid-19 commit suicide - the opinion of doctors
claims: During the Covid-19 pandemic in Ukraine, cases of suicides during the treatment of coronavirus and after it were increasingly recorded.
In 2020 alone, more than 10 people who had a severe form of Covid-19, learned about the diagnosis or had already fallen ill, committed suicide.

Psychiatrist Tatiana Pyatkovskaya and neurologist Anna Kulish told ICTV Facts what diseases can be the cause of obsessive thoughts in a patient after Covid-19 and how to deal with it so that after the disease the nervous system was normal.
The cause of suicidal thoughts and suicides may be a response to the pandemic as a whole.
Prolonged isolation and a number of psychological factors influence the occurrence of suicidal thoughts.
The hypoxic state in severe patients disrupts normal brain function, which causes cognitive changes.
Microthrombosis of the brain vessels, which causes Covid-19, also disrupts its work.
Family relationships are one of the causes of suicide.
Stress and fear often provoke the emergence of negative thoughts.
Any somatic disease that proceeds in severe form can cause thoughts of suicide, since in this case the stress reaction can induce depressive disorders, sometimes leading to suicidal thoughts.
Neurological diseases that can push to suicide include Multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease.
During or after coronavirus, Multiple sclerosis may progress, causing numbness and weakness of the limbs, impaired vision, impaired speech and swallowing.
Parkinson's disease disrupts the work of neurotransmitters in the body, which leads to depression.
Asthenia is a psychopathological disorder that is manifested by general fatigue, decreased working capacity, sleep problems, pronounced irritability, vegetative failures.
Depression is a disease that increased during the pandemic.
Relatives and friends should support the patient or a person who has fallen ill, rather than reproach or criticize them.
People should look for new hobbies to do something and have a desire to live.
It is important to communicate more with a person who has signs of mental or neurological diseases and support them so that people do not feel lonely.
In the case of suicidal thoughts, it is necessary to clearly differentiate when it is necessary to consult a neurologist, and when it is necessary to consult a psychiatrist.

To reduce the risk of suicide, it is necessary to control the course of chronic diseases, monitor moral state, keep positive views, lead a healthy lifestyle, and contact a psychologist, psychotherapist or psychiatrist if necessary.
Since the beginning of the year, 123 teenagers have committed suicide in Ukraine.
The cause of child deaths is the lack of control by parents of social networks, where children often fall into the so-called “death groups”.

c13c0b13-7e15-433f-a22e-fcf9e6ad56e1.title: Slowing down coronavirus pandemic makes oceans quieter, good for whales
claims: HESAVEK, Iceland is a small town surrounded by snow-capped mountain ranges.
The northern coast of Iceland has become the “whale capital” of the country.
Whale watching is the most popular activity for visitors in Iceland.
Heimer Harderson has led humans into the ocean for nearly 30 years to meet some of the largest animals in the world.
The number of visitors to Iceland has been severely affected by the Coronavirus pandemic.
The global slowdown in growth has benefited whales as human intervention has diminished.
Ambient noise in the oceans from cruise ships and Sonar Building collapses has decreased.
Ari Friedlander, a marine ecologist and biologist, studies how calmer oceans affect whales by measuring their stress levels with hormone samples.
Animals use acoustics, such as whale songs, to communicate with each other and search for food.
Noise in the environment can interfere with communication and other important life functions of whales.
Reducing human activity and noisy environment decreases stress hormone levels in whales.
Stress affects whales in the same way as humans, altering their behavior and ability to act both physically and mentally.
Stress can lead to long-term changes that affect the overall health of the whale and its ability to reproduce.
The epidemic helped accelerate the cessation of commercial whaling off the coast of Iceland.
Iceland is one of three countries in the world where commercial whaling is still allowed, along with Japan and Norway.
Two Icelandic whaling companies stopped hunting due to health restrictions last year.
Demand for whale meat continues to decline in Iceland.
Most of the demand for whale meat in Iceland came from tourists who wanted to try it during their visits.
Icelanders have redefined their relationship with whales in recent decades.
Tourism has helped people realize that whales are more valuable alive than dead.
Whale watching tours also affect animals, but the experience helps motivate people to protect them.
Heimer Harderson hopes that whale watching will again become big business, helping to support the animals and the entire city.

f00d1496-353e-407b-b13a-b71893ace576.title: Scientists have told how global warming has affected agriculture
claims: Global warming has led to an average decrease in crop yields by 21% over the past 60 years.

a78ad177-1e20-4960-b8f1-be8e7362ff7a.title: Two new parks opened in Khimki

2515e9fc-2550-464b-930e-11d50f9d917b.title: The launch of the spacecraft Crew Dragon (Crew-2) with astronauts to the ISS due to the weather was postponed to April 23
claims: NASA and SpaceX announced the postponement of the launch of the mission to change the crew of the ISS Crew-2, also known as USCV-2 (US Crew Vehicle 2): it was shifted by only one day — on April 23.
The reason for the transfer is adverse weather conditions.

Launch Update @ NASA and @ SpaceX now are targeting Friday, April 23 at 5: 49 a.m. ET for the launch of the Crew-2 mission to the @ Space _ Station due to unfavorable weather conditions along the flight path on Thursday.

The Crew-2 mission is distinguished by the fact that SpaceX uses the restored first stage of the Falcon 9 and the Crew Dragon spacecraft - the stage with the inventory number B1061.2, which launched the Crew-1 mission, and the C206 Endeavour spacecraft, which flew to the ISS as part of the first demo mission Demo-2.
This will be the first manned flight on a rocket and a ship that has already flown into space.
In June 2020, NASA allowed SpaceX to reuse the Crew Dragon capsule and the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket to deliver astronauts to the ISS.
The Crew-2 rocket and spacecraft have already passed all checks, they are installed vertically on the LC-39A launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The company of Elon Musk has long used already flying ships and the first stages of the Falcon 9 rocket to deliver cargo under the Commercial Resupply Services contract.
The current record for reusable Falcon 9 is nine restarts of the same first stage.

Crew-2 is SpaceX ’ s second full-time mission to send people to the ISS as part of its ongoing contact with NASA and its Commercial Crew Program, aimed at supporting commercial companies engaged in the development of space vehicles.
At least four more missions are planned.

The Crew-2 crew was announced back in July 2020 — two NASA astronauts (Robert Shane Kimbro and Catherine Megan MacArthur) and one each from ESA (Tom Pesquet) and JAXA (Akihiko Hoshide) will go to the ISS.
They will be part of the ISS-65 / 66 expedition.
The duration of this mission will be 180 days.

On April 5, 2020, NASA and SpaceX successfully redocked the Crew Dragon spacecraft of the Crew-1 mission for the first time from the IDA-1 docking node to IDA-3 to make room for the Crew-2 mission spacecraft.
When Crew-2 arrives on the ISS, the crew of the station until May 9 will consist of 11 people.

a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1.title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
claims: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere

In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.
Hemingway's creative style is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.
Hemingway uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor to interpret his own creative style.

Qian Zhongshu's theory states that a metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, but also different.
Hemingway often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, only admiring Shakespeare and Tolstoy.
Hemingway used boxing as a metaphor to compare himself with other writers, saying he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, but chose to play with Turgenev first.

Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp, because the ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.

Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius", and Hemingway was indeed a genius.

claims: NASA said today that the Mars rover "perseverance" continues to make history, yesterday successfully converted carbon dioxide into oxygen in the Martian atmosphere, the first successful oxygenation on another planet.

Perseverance uses the Mars Oxygen In situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) built in front of its right and designed by MIT to produce oxygen.
MOXIE is a car battery-sized gold box that uses electricity and chemical properties to break down carbon dioxide molecules and successfully produce oxygen.
Since carbon dioxide is composed of 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms, the by-product of MOXIE's oxygen production is carbon monoxide.
MOXIE can produce oxygen for future astronauts to breathe on Mars, and also need not drag a large amount of oxygen from Earth as a propellant in the future.
MOXIE's first score was to produce 5 grams of oxygen, equivalent to the amount an astronaut needs to breathe for 10 minutes of normal activity.
MOXIE was originally designed to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour, and engineers will now conduct more experiments to try to increase production.
MOXIE is made of heat-resistant materials such as nickel alloys, which can withstand high temperatures of 800 degrees Celsius.
The thin gold coating on the top of MOXIE ensures that it will not cause damage to the car’s Perseverance.
MIT engineer Michael Hecht said the one-ton version of MOXIE could produce about 25 tons of oxygen needed for a rocket to launch from Mars.
Since 96% of the Martian atmosphere is carbon dioxide, producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere is much more feasible than extracting ice from the Martian surface.

claims: Climate change has directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.

High temperatures can lead to the formation of ozone close to the ground, decreasing lung function.
Extreme weather events like floods and storms can bring hidden risks to human health, including injuries and death.
Heavy rainfall and flooding can increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks in polluted waters.
Climate change has lengthened the pollen season in Germany, exacerbating respiratory diseases like asthma and allergic rhinitis.

Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus.
Globalization increases the risk of disease transmission through imported goods and infected travelers.
High temperatures, carbon dioxide, and changing rainfall patterns can affect plant growth and crop yields.

Climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes like northern Europe, but negative implications for tropical and subtropical regions.

The cost of limiting global warming is less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.
Rising temperatures increase the risk of irreversible damage.
Human-made greenhouse gas emissions are the main cause of temperature rise since the industrial era.
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions can limit the development of global warming.

58655f0a-17b2-4baf-aef6-08f061b6b0c2.title: How did Klimt ’ s paintings influence the modern ideas that emerged in Vienna in 1900?
claims: Ronald Lauder, an Austrian expressionist art collector and co-founder of Neue Galerie, bought a single painting, Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer, for a staggering US $135 million in 2006.

Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer was painted by Klimt in 1907 and reflects the characteristics of Vienna at the turn of the century: the richness of content, the sensuality of color, and the vast energy of innovation.

Klimt was a skilled painter in the tradition of the 19th century New Art, but his painting, Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer, has a new historical significance: it is Klimt’s first painting to leave the traditional three-dimensional space and turn to the brightly decorated modern flat space.
Klimt’s painting, Lady Adele I, expresses Lady Adele’s irresistible beauty and lust, its exquisite decoration and exotic theme, and takes the lead in announcing the birth of modernity.
Klimt used the painting to create a secular icon that would later represent the expectations of an entire generation in Vienna at the end of the 19th century.

Klimt gave up on his attempts to bring the world of three-dimensional space to the canvas of two-dimensional space in a more realistic way, and instead pursued the real phenomenon hidden behind the camera that cannot be captured by the camera.

Klimt and several younger protégés, including Koxica and Schiller, turned the artist’s point of view inward, away from the external world of three degrees, towards the multi-dimensional inner self and the unconscious mind.
Modern science, especially modern biology, influenced Klimt’s artistic expression, just as they influenced much of the culture of Vienna in the 1900s.
After reading Darwin’s work, Klimt became fascinated with cellular structures, the building blocks of all living things, and used bio-inspired fertility symbols in his painting, Lady Adele.
The jigsaw puzzle of Lady Adele’s clothes is not just like Art Nouveau decorations, but rather, they are symbols of male and female cells: rectangular sperm and oval eggs.

Klimt started his career as a fine but commonplace painter, following the history and popular style of his master, Hans Makart, and did some decorative work for theatres, museums, and other public buildings.
Klimt’s paintings took a bold and original turn in 1886, when he and his colleague Franz von Matsch went to paint commemorative paintings for the old Castle Theatre.

Klimt painted specific audience members that could be identified from the direction of the stage, and these audience members do not look like they are watching the opera performance, but they are performing their own inner play.

Freud began using hypnosis and psychotherapy to treat patients suffering from hysteria, and connected the patient’s hysterical symptoms with his past traumatic experiences, around the same time Klimt did his work.

The characteristic intuition of Klimt’s later works developed in parallel with Freud’s psychological studies, and foretold the trend to the depths of the heart, which eventually swept through the various fields of Vienna in the 1900s.
The stage that gave birth to Viennese modernism was characterized by an attempt to break with the past and explore new ways of expression in art, architecture, psychology, literature, and music.
