f3320f28-8541-4736-8cfb-4a7bc22429eb.title: What are the requirements of planting pattern in Iran?
claims: According to Mehr News Agency, the pattern of cultivation in recent years has been one of the most challenging issues raised in the field of agriculture in Iran.
The surplus production of tomatoes, onions and some other products has highlighted the lack of precise implementation of the cultivation pattern in Iran.
Experts want to pay attention to the experiences of other countries in the field of cultivation pattern and use it to accurately implement the cultivation pattern in Iran.
Cultivation pattern refers to the area under cultivation of different crops in different time periods.
Cultivation pattern shows the time and spatial order or sequence of crops or the marking of a particular crop field.
The change in the proportion of the land under cultivation of different crops as well as the change in the temporal and spatial order of crops is called the cultivation pattern.
Time sequence is the rotation of crops or in other words the rotation of crops, for example, soybeans after winter wheat in temperate areas.
Location sequence is the cultivation of crops in a specific location, for example, the cultivation of corn and potatoes in the vicinity.

Iran has a variety of ecological agricultural areas that are suitable for different cultivation patterns including different products, such as oilseeds, legumes, root plants, vegetables and animal feed.
Monoculture refers to the cultivation of the same crop over the years without changing or rotating the crop planted on that land.
If a crop is cultivated during a season and the season after that and the seasons after that, it can be said that the pattern of cultivation is monoculture in terms of the time sequence.
If more than one crop is grown in a single year, it is called multiple crops.

The technical and scientific requirements and facilities required for the development and implementation of the pattern of cultivation depend on the type of crop, the fertility of the land, and the availability of other natural resources.
Indonesia and China have been successful in developing and implementing the culture pattern, with mixed, row by row cultivation of maize and potatoes being a common practice.
Australia has also been successful, with mung beans widely planted with summer and winter cereals.
China has common practices of rotation cultivation of wheat with corn, wheat with soybeans, wheat with rice, and rapeseed with rice.
The FAO supports its member countries in developing and implementing cultivation patterns through the implementation of various field projects.
The GEF7 project, currently being implemented in China, aims to support various crop cultivation patterns to increase crop yields and improve crop stability.
Adopting different cropping patterns for agricultural production has various advantages, including increasing the productivity of arable land and improving the livelihood of farmers.
The combined cultivation of legumes with cereals can improve soil fertility due to the role of legumes in the stabilization of nitrogen in the soil.
The implementation of the rotation or mixed culture pattern can disrupt the cycle of diseases and pests.

Governments can encourage farmers to practice cultivation patterns by implementing various facilitative and empowering policies, including financial incentives and providing services and maintenance costs for mechanized agriculture.
The availability and availability of a variety of different crops suitable for farmers is necessary for the implementation of the cultivation pattern.
Capacity building and awareness for farmers and agricultural promoters is also necessary for the implementation of the cultivation pattern.
The feasibility of planting patterns in Iran is possible, with the country having diverse ecological agricultural areas suitable for different cultivation patterns.

Iran needs to develop and implement a culture model, with requirements including access to advanced technologies and equipment, germplasm of some crops, and human power capacity in the agricultural sector.

The implementation of the cultivation model in Iran can meet the country's need for strategic products such as wheat, sugar, oil and livestock inputs, but it can have economic and environmental costs.

Empowerment policies, including financial support, investment in agriculture, and the empowerment of personnel and manpower involved in the agricultural sector, are necessary for the success of the cultivation model.
Encouraging farmers to participate enthusiastically for their own benefit is key to the success and sustainability of the cultivation model.

At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.

Hemingway has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist.

The study was conducted between 1395 and 1396, and the researchers conducted in-depth interviews with 21 married women in Karaj who had a history of cosmetic surgery.

The criteria for selecting the study participants were: at least one year after their cosmetic surgery, their surgery was done solely for cosmetic reasons, and they had no medical and restorative reasons, and they were satisfied to participate in the research.
The cosmetic surgeries in this study were all cosmetic surgeries without medical necessity, such as nose, eyelid, eyebrow, cheek, forehead, neck, flank, buttocks and various forms of sculpture.

Those who participated in the study were between 23 and 58 years old, and the education was six people with a diploma and below, four people with an associate degree, nine people with a bachelor ’ s degree and two people with a master ’ s degree.
In terms of income, seven were excellent, eight were good, four were average, and two were poor.
Twelve lived in private housing, seven in rental housing and two in institutional housing.
Nine of them were housewives and 11 were employed.

Individual factors affecting beauty practices include negative self-concept, social isolation, deformity, experience of neurotic symptoms, tendency to narcissistic personality pattern, need for approval and variety seeking and fear and avoiding the symptoms of aging.

Family-marital factors that played a role in cosmetic surgery include perception of repetition for the spouse, attention of the spouse, history of cosmetic surgery in the family, degrading behavior of the spouse and other family members, increased sexual satisfaction, decreased marital intimacy, and positive attitude and encouragement of the spouse.

Socio-cultural factors effective in performing cosmetic surgeries include the role of peers and friends, receiving social approval, the value of beauty and morphology, the role of media models, facilitating the practice of surgery and the progress of cosmetic surgery, and the fashion of surgery.
The greater the pressure of peers and friends, the more media, as well as receiving social approval, the greater the likelihood of cosmetic surgery.
The study has limitations, including that the study population includes only married women in Karaj, and the results cannot be generalized.
Cosmetic surgery may result from other factors and variables that have not been identified in this study.

The results of this research have been published as a scientific research paper in the journal "Skin and Beauty" affiliated to the Center for the Education and Research of Skin and Leprosy Diseases of Tehran University of Medical Sciences.

27 percent of women reported an increase in mental health problems, compared with just 10 percent of men.

Data from Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs shows that the percentage of employed women has fallen twice as much as men.
Nine million people are working in Japan, down 3.2 percent from a year ago, and a decline of more than two-thirds of women is reported in the fall.
Domestic violence hotlines encountered more calls as family members were forced to stay together in quarantine.

The epidemic has brought about many changes in children’s social development and has been responsible for hidden parental stress, which doctors say may lead to parental neglect.

Japan is one of the few countries to provide timely information on suicide as it is a major social issue in the island nation.

claims: Four people, including two children, drowned in the English Channel between France and Britain on Tuesday, October 27.
A boat carrying refugees bound for Britain had capsized in the English Channel, resulting in the deaths of a woman and a man, along with two children aged 5 and 8.
Nearly 20 refugees, most of them Iranian nationals, were on the boat when it capsized.
Rescue operations began on Tuesday morning to transport the survivors to a hospital, but a man drowned and died before the rescue, followed by a woman and two children who died of cardiac arrest.
15 of the rescued refugees are Iranian and have been placed in medical facilities in the port of Calais and the city of Dunkirk, among them a seriously ill man.
The search for the other passengers was halted by nightfall, and the Dunkirk city prosecutor and border police are still investigating the cause of the boat's sinking.
The first investigation by local authorities found that the boat was carrying between 19 and 20 people and that the weather at the waterway was bad.
French Interior Minister's representative for citizenship, Marlene Schiapa, tweeted that she was deeply saddened by the news and will work with the UK authorities to prevent such incidents.

British Prime Minister Boris Johnson expressed sympathy for the families of the victims and stressed that the British government, along with the French authorities, will fight the smuggling gangs that prepare the dangerous journey of these vulnerable people.
Thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries attempt to cross the Channel each year, with 2358 people rescued by boat to the coast of France or the United Kingdom in 2019 alone.
The Channel between France and Britain has seen a surge in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 2018, resulting in accidents and loss of lives.

The number of people on board the sinking boat is reported to be either 19 or 28, including Iranian and Iraqi individuals.
A French rescue helicopter pulled Rasoul Irannejad, 35, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, and two children, Anita, 9, and Armin, 6, out of the water, but they died.
The Irannejad family had left Iran in the summer and traveled to Turkey, then Italy, and finally France, with the goal of reaching the UK.
The family had attempted to cross the border into the UK twice before the final attempt, hoping to earn £100 a day and pay back loans.
Immigration laws have been tightened in the UK, and safe routes to enter and declare asylum have been closed due to the coronavirus epidemic.
At least 7,400 people have made their way to the UK via the English Channel this year, four times the number of people who entered the UK illegally last year.
The cost of crossing the Channel for refugees is between 5,000 and 6,000 euros per person.
The Irannejad family paid almost 8,000 euros per person to cross from Turkey to Italy and then to France.
The total cost for the family to reach the UK would have been at least €13,000 per person.

8f6f06c9-bf09-484e-9b60-c5e5c5b33372.title: Japan warns: Suicide kills more people than coronavirus

5e54b5e5-d77f-491b-ad88-198f339c2dd5.title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
claims: France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.
Seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel since the beginning of the year.
Britain’s interior minister, Priti Patel, and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.

d35cb1c3-06ee-4116-bf06-ae398c64fb8b.title: In Japan, suicide kills more people than coronavirus

The coronavirus epidemic has led to an increase in suicide rates in Japan.
Suicide rates have been higher among women in Japan during the coronavirus outbreak.
The suicide rate among women in Japan increased by almost 83 percent in October 2020 compared to last October.
Suicide rates among men in Japan increased by almost 22 percent over the same period.
Women are more likely than men to be laid off in jobs that are at greater risk of being laid off, such as part-time hotel workers, the food service industry, and the retail industry.
A study by the international non-profit organization CARE found that 27 percent more women reported mental health problems during the coronavirus epidemic.
Only 10% of men reported mental health problems during the coronavirus epidemic.
The suicide death rate in Japan was 18.5 per 100,000 people in 2016.
The annual global average of suicide death rate is 10.6 per 100,000 people.

99981532-c91e-4227-9319-b8ddd5047f2d.title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
claims: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.
There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.
A team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.
The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.
The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA’s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.
Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.
The device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.
Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.

Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said water-soluble perchlorates are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.
The study is based on data from NASA’s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.

Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.
NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.
The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.

2aeeac7c-7ffe-4f3e-bd71-8204045d6bb0.title: When does the dream of Mars become a reality?
claims: Earth is the only human habitable planet that has ever maintained its unchallenged sovereignty.

The surface of Mars is not suitable for humans and most living things due to the very low air pressure, an atmosphere with only 1% oxygen, and the lack of liquid water.

The temperature of Mars at low latitudes is similar to that of Antarctica.
A sun-based day on Mars is 24 hours, 39 minutes, and 35.3244 seconds.
The surface of Mars is only 28.4% less than the surface of Earth.

Mars has a significant amount of all the elements necessary to sustain terrestrial life.
The cost of a trip to Mars is estimated at around $6 billion to $500 billion.
Living on Mars is a dream that scientists at NASA and other space agencies have been working for years to achieve.
The planet’s surface conditions and the presence of water make it the only option on the table for life outside of Earth.

40eafe81-14b6-4b89-8400-437c70f581ae.title: Interesting and surprising facts about Mars and its prerequisites for habitation + Pictures
claims: Living in a place other than Earth has become one of the major concerns of scientists over the years.

7e329b52-9cb4-4952-96b9-f6f60168550c.title: Couples misconceptions about the effects of cosmetic surgery

48e8e0b8-d557-4bdb-9529-a343340127e1.title: Climate change is a wake-up call for global agriculture.
claims: Climate change has changed the conditions of crop growth and made its future unpredictable in most parts of the world.
Small farmland, which accounts for about 90 percent of the world’s 570 million farmland, is particularly vulnerable to seasonal climate change.
The land that families have used for generations may suddenly become uncultivated due to climate change.
Phenomena such as the El Niño Southern Oscillation can cause rainfall or droughts that destroy crops.
The flooding of the Nzoia River in Kenya in May 2020 caused flooding in western Kenya, destroying homes, schools, roads, bridges, and farmland of more than 32 square kilometers.
Farmers in Iran face similar problems in the face of periods of drought and flooding.
Recent severe droughts and heavy floods in the Middle East have destroyed much of the food supply.
Sporadic rainfall cycles can reduce yields and lead to secondary impacts that worsen the food security situation, such as wildfires.
Financial and social inequality make climate-related food security issues more difficult.
Many small farmland farmers are poor and food insecure.
Climate change plays a key role as catalysts in problems that already exist in the field of resources, affecting the quality and quantity of food produced and how it is distributed equally.
About a third of the world’s soil is partly or very degraded, and the situation is getting worse overall.
Unsustainable farming practices harm soil health, and some are caused by climate change.
Warm temperatures are associated with the rapid loss of soil organic matter, which is the major store of food and energy for soil microbes.

Climate change is reshaping the relationships between crops, pests, pathogens, and weeds, exacerbating a variety of trends, including a decline in insect pollination and an increase in water scarcity.
Climate change has created problems with the availability of water resources for agriculture, including changing rainfall patterns, seasonal snow melt, and saltwater intrusion into coastal aquifers.
Short-term reforms pose long-term problems about the role of humans in reducing soil health and the unpredictability of crops.
Problems such as poverty, hunger, government corruption, and lack of education contribute to food insecurity issues around the world.
Expanding agricultural activity can release more greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, as soak land and land exposed to seasonal floods store more carbon than productive land.
The use of fertilizer can cause damage to the environment in the long run, including the release of nitrous oxide into the atmosphere.
Food security in the future is unlikely to lessen the impact of climate change on farmers, given that more countries are lagging behind climate targets.
Water availability continues to be a problem in expanding existing farmland and creating new farmland.
Climate impact is a major factor in reducing food security, but other factors, such as maintaining equality and economic stability, could play a role in the future of global food supply.
Human migration is related to multi-year droughts, political instability, and falling incomes, which forced people to migrate to find ways to support their families.
Socio-political factors and an understanding of the vulnerability of populations are more important than climate change in driving farmers to migrate to new areas.
Smart agricultural policies should take into account vulnerabilities beyond climate change and socio-economic content.

1d5c736b-083a-42c0-a27c-6f57ca775bd2.title: Climate change and 21% reduction in agricultural productivity
claims: Cornell University in the US led a new study that found farms have averaged 21 percent less yields over the past six decades as a result of climate change.
This equates to a total loss of seven years of agricultural productivity growth.
Global agriculture is increasingly exposed to the effects of climate change, with warmer places such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most.
Agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34%.
Experts developed a comprehensive econometric model to quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on total factor productivity.
Climate-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity.
Climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years.
The group considered more than 200 systematic changes from the econometric model, and the results were largely consistent.
The historical impacts of climate change have been greatest in areas that have become warmer, including areas of Africa, Latin America and Asia.
The study was published in the journal Nature Climate Change.

736ae444-d7cc-4f58-8db8-ef94608744c8.title: How does NASA build a base with breathable air on Mars?
claims: NASA is planning to send humans to Mars and needs to build a base with breathable air on the planet.
The window of opportunity to send humans to Mars occurs every 26 months when the planet is closest to Earth.
The plans for Mars are to send the infrastructure first, and then after 26 months, send the crew.
Sending infrastructure to Mars includes building power plants, a habitat, rovers, and vehicles.
The production of oxygen is a major problem to deal with when building a Martian base.
The habitat will require small amounts of oxygen, but other components like rocket propellants will require much more oxygen.
About 30 tons of oxygen are needed to get astronauts off the surface of Mars and into orbit.
Taking 30 tons of oxygen to Mars would delay the mission by about a decade, so a better solution is to produce oxygen on Mars.
NASA is working on a concept called In-situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) to produce oxygen on Mars using the planet's resources.
The ISRU concept involves using a device called MOXIE to pick up carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere and produce oxygen.
MOXIE is a miniature version of a larger device that uses a fuel cell-like technology to produce oxygen.
The MOXIE device was successfully landed on Mars in February 2021 as part of the Endurance rover mission.
The biggest challenge in building the MOXIE device was energy consumption, as the rover has limited power.
The MOXIE device operates on very small amounts of energy, similar to the energy used to light a light bulb.
NASA engineers are collecting data from MOXIE to test its performance in the Martian environment.
The data collected from MOXIE is relatively simple and can be analyzed quickly, in just a few days.
If MOXIE is successful, it will demonstrate the practicality of the ISRU principle on Mars and pave the way for larger-scale oxygen production.
Another essential resource needed to survive on Mars is water, which is necessary for humans to drink and to produce hydrogen and carbon dioxide compounds.
Water can be extracted from the Martian soil or from ice deposits at the planet's poles.
One concept for solving the water problem is to map the location of water ice on Mars and extract it from the soil or ice deposits.
Another way to extract water is from minerals in the Martian soil, such as gypsum and Epsom salts.
Perchlorate is a toxic substance found in large quantities on Mars, but it has chemical properties that make it useful for producing energy.
According to Michael Hackett, perchlorate makes up 1% of the Martian soil and has incredible amounts of energy.

2f73c974-c00c-4f77-a49d-42125c4e0c3b.title: The Mars rover produced oxygen from the atmosphere for the first time.
claims: The Mars rover produced oxygen from the atmosphere for the first time.
The Perseverance Rover converted some of the carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere into oxygen during the first test of the scientific instrument MOXIE.
MOXIE stands for the term oxygen experiment in situ from Martian sources.
Maxi produced about 5.4 grams of oxygen after heating the scientific instrument for about 2 hours.
5.4 grams of oxygen is enough to keep an astronaut alive for about 10 minutes.
The thin atmosphere on Mars has 96% carbon dioxide and is not suitable for human respiration.
Maxi works by splitting carbon dioxide molecules, which consist of one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms.
Maxi separates and stores oxygen molecules and emits carbon monoxide as waste.
Converting carbon dioxide to oxygen requires a temperature of 800 ° C.
Maxi uses heat-resistant materials, such as gold plating and aerogel, to prevent heat radiation and damage to various parts of the rover.
Jim Reuter, director of NASA’s Space Technology Mission Directorate, said this is the first critical step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars.
Oxygen is not only used for breathing, but rocket propellants are also dependent on it.
To launch four astronauts from the surface of Mars, it would take about 6,800 kilograms of rocket fuel and 24,950 kilograms of oxygen.
Astronauts who spend a year on the surface of Mars could use a ton of oxygen.
Getting that much oxygen from Earth to Mars would be difficult and expensive.
An oxygen exchanger weighing about 1 ton, the next generation and more powerful than Maxi, could produce enough oxygen in the long run.
Maxi will likely produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour from the Martian atmosphere in future experiments.
The scientific instrument will conduct about nine more experiments over the next two years.
Maxi’s technology could help future astronauts live on the surface of the planet and use the resources around them.
Trudy Kortes, director of the technology show at NASA's Space Technology Mission Directorate, said Maxi is not just the first tool to generate oxygen from the resources of another world.
Maxi takes Mars’ resources and processes them into usable materials such as propellants, breathable air, or combined with hydrogen into water.
Positive results from these experiments will bring Mars missions like Elon Musk’s Mars project one step closer to landing humans on the Red Planet.

1e39c7d0-89a1-4590-9556-d67a78b9903e.title: The need to protect communities against the psychological consequences of all
claims: Undoubtedly, these days, the “mental health crisis ” is another epidemic that has plagued the world with the COVID-19 epidemic, raising concerns about the increased risk of suicide, especially among young people, due to the problems and limitations of the spread of the disease in different parts of the world.
Data from past epidemics suggest a direct and significant link between the occurrence of epidemics and the rise in suicide.
The Toronto Transit Commission in Canada reported that suicide attempts or deaths rose by almost a third in the first eight months of the epidemic.

There are many risk factors for suicide that are associated with the epidemic, including: anxiety and fear of family members, financial pressures, reduced social interactions with friends and social activities, interruptions in life goals and daily activities, feelings of hopelessness and helplessness, increased family stress due to remote work and home schooling, increased family fighting and conflict.
Preliminary data suggest a decline in national suicide rates in 2020 in some countries, including the United States.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show that the total suicide rate in the United States fell by 5.6% in 2020.

A study published in the Lancet Psychiatry Journal found that suicide cases in middle and high-income countries remained largely unchanged or were lower than expected during the first months of the COVID-19 epidemic.
The study included national data from 10 countries and data from 25 specific regions in 11 countries.
The report found no evidence of an increase in suicide cases in any of the countries surveyed.
There is also evidence in 12 countries or regions that suicide cases are lower than expected.

Jane Pirkis, director of the Centre for Mental Health at the University of Melbourne and senior author of the study, said: “We need to continue monitoring the data and be more vigilant about any increase in suicide rates, especially with the emergence of the full economic consequences of the epidemic.

Increasing mental health services and suicide prevention programs and providing safe financial networks may help prevent the possible and long-term damaging effects of the epidemic on suicidal tendencies.

The researchers also warned of some signals that the epidemic could affect suicide rates in low- and middle-income countries, although the data was only available to a small minority of these countries.
Japan’s Ministry of Health and Welfare said on January 22 that according to preliminary data, about 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7 percent from the previous year.
Last year was the first year in more than a decade that suicide rates in Japan increased, with women and children taking the largest share.

bef68460-e590-4dc8-83be-67cb5084b3db.title: How ‘ Pandemic ’ Increases Suicide Risk in Medical Assistants / Strategies to Increase Resilience
claims: Facing the death of patients, being away from family and loved ones, high work pressure, and anxiety about illness and death, is a big part of the daily life of the medical staff.

Dr. Mehdi Eskandari points to failure to explain what happens before suicide, telling ISNA: In general, when people’s desires do not match their own and there is a gap between them, people experience feelings of failure.
Being in a pandemic situation increases the level of failure.

Some factors, such as having a history of suicide or having suicidal thoughts and a depressed life, can affect suicide attempts, and in this situation, the risk of these people to commit suicide is more than others.
Lack of problem solving and questioning attitude can also be effective factors in the occurrence of suicide.
The medical staff in this pandemic faced more death than any other human being, which increases the risk of suicide.
Job isolation, fear of infection, and the suffering of people on their deathbed all increase the risk of suicide.
Having a space full of fun and laughter and creating vitality makes the resilience very high.
Close relationships with loved ones also contribute greatly to resilience.

Dr. Maryam Hanasabzadeh Esfahani said that withdrawal from friendship and family gatherings is a risk factor that increases the incidence of suicide.

Lack of or lack of social support in this very difficult period will certainly be effective in increasing the risk of suicide.
Improving financial conditions can be important in preventing suicide attempts, according to Dr. Hanasabzadeh Esfahani.

Having social networks and support, learning problem-solving skills, and the availability of a psychologist or counselor are protective factors against suicide.

d2527482-f75e-4888-bc9c-beed0028ead9.title: Stories of the iceberg.
claims: Some experts in world fiction literature believe that the turning point in the influence of Ernest Hemingway, the world famous writer in modern literature, was a theory that he himself invented in world fiction.
The “iceberg ” theory was a new mode of narrative that made the writing less intense and the reader ’ s imagination flaring.
The hallmark of iceberg stories is not telling a large part of the story and leaving it to the audience to think more and become curious.
Hemingway likened such short stories to an iceberg whose bulk is hidden underwater, and said that the glory of the movement of the iceberg is only seen in the one-eighth of the water.

The collection of stories of Parviz Shishegaran or flash fiction in the book "Ticket for sale at the end of the metro line" is very similar to the style of iceberg and is a prominent example of such stories.
Each of the stories depicts a slice of the lives of combatants and minutes of people ’ s lives during and after the war, which not only makes us not tired, but also makes us curious.

In the story of the "ticket sale of the last station of the subway line", the subject of which dates back to the post-war years, we are faced with a veteran who needs oxygen in the congestion and crowds of passengers inside one of the Tehran subway due to respiratory problems caused by war injuries and before the oxygen arrives.
One of the defining features of iceberg stories is that they are visual, so Hemingway has had the chance to make multiple films out of most of his stories.
So a successful writer is one who creates the most pictorial scenes with the least number of sentences and satisfies the reader.

Parviz Shishegaran has done this in this collection and has delivered good stories to the audience, and the turning point of the stories of this book is their brilliant beginning and effective ending.

The structure of the stories in this book is based on the same theory of the iceberg, but in this book the author did not pay attention to space building and in some narratives narrated the story and quickly rejected.
This small book was published in 43 pages by Amirkabir Publications.

a548a9eb-6840-4375-8c64-5392b68a547f.title: Climate crisis threatens a third of global food production
claims: Global warming continues at its current pace, food production areas will see significant changes in rainfall and temperature.
If the temperature rises to about 3.7 ° C and if the increase in greenhouse gas emissions is forecast, the food growing areas will see an increase in temperature and change in rainfall patterns.
About 95 percent of current crop production takes place in areas defined as having a healthy climate, or in conditions where temperatures, precipitation and drought fall within certain boundaries.
If temperatures rise to 3.7 ° C or so by the end of the century, safe zones will decline dramatically, most notably in South and Southeast Asia and sub-Saharan Africa.
If greenhouse gas emissions are reduced or the Paris climate agreement is met, about half to eight percent of food production could be at risk.
The Paris Agreement aims to raise temperatures between 1.5 and 2 percent Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
Further increases in temperature will pose a risk to crops, and many areas are likely to face water shortages, according to the report.
Researchers examined the effects of climate change on 27 critically important food crops and seven livestock species.
Global warming will increase if greenhouse gases continue to rise by the end of the last century.
Global warming has already had an impact on agricultural production.

aacf9bce-c0f6-4c24-8b32-12a22c6de564.title: Determining the Model of Low Water and High Yield Cultivation in Arak University
claims: Scientists at Arak University determined the appropriate cultivation pattern for the crops of the plains of the Markazi province to reduce the harvest from non-renewable water resources and achieve maximum productivity and profit.
The project was carried out in collaboration with the Faculty of Agriculture and Environment of Arak University and the Agricultural Jihad Organization of Markazi Province.
Dr. Mohammad Javad Nahniya, Dr. Hossein Salehi Arjmand, Engineer Sharafi, and Engineer Akbari were part of the project team.
The project studied the effects of climate change on crops, including soil acidity, salinity, organic carbon, organic matter, soil losses, and erosion of different areas.
The project obtained results on the current conditions and cultivation pattern of Shazand, Khomein, and Saveh plains through field testing and data analysis.
The project predicted the effects of climate change on the cultivation pattern of Shazand, Khomein, and Saveh plains.
A mathematical model of water allocation planning was developed based on 10-day periods.

The project investigated the increase in income and productivity by optimizing the cultivation pattern proportional to the quantity and quality of water and chemical and physical characteristics of soil.
The project led to operational planning for the implementation of appropriate cultivation and irrigation patterns in Shazand, Saveh, and Khomein plains.
The project combined water and dryland products and surface, underground, and rainfall water resources in a pattern.
The combination of water and land in a single decision matrix led to the use of the concept of tiling in ranking optimal responses in the agricultural sector.

4b69a7c1-30d3-4ed2-aef7-72cde5a7474b.title: China's "artificial sun" record
claims: China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.
The artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.

China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.
The Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.
The artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.
Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.
The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.
The Tokamak HL-2m device in Chengdu maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.
The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China’s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.
Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.
China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.
These facilities are called “artificial suns” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.
When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.
To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.
Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.
Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.
The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.
China joined the ITER project in 2003.

claims: Vladimir Mayakovsky was born on June 19, 1893, in a village in the Caucasus.
